commissions.title: Commissions
commissions.lede: Site-specific work in cement, plaster, and steel — developed with architects, designers, and private collectors from first sketch to final install. Interior or exterior, one piece or a full program.

sections.body:
Every commission begins with a conversation about the space, the aesthetic, and the experience the finished piece is meant to create.

Commissioned work can be found in private collections, hospitality, and commercial spaces across the country. Every commission is unique, inspired by its setting and built to endure.

sections.heading: 01 — Consultation
sections.body: A conversation about the site, scale, and use — in person or by video, with reference material from prior work.

sections.heading: 02 — Concept
sections.body: A direction, material palette, and quote — refined until the form, vision, and budget align.

sections.heading: 03 — Fabrication
sections.body: Designed, created, and finished in studio — with progress photos shared as the piece develops.

sections.heading: 04 — Install
sections.body: Delivered and installed on site throughout the U.S. and internationally.

sections.heading: Five stages
sections.body: Five stages, in order. The first two are mine to control; the last three belong partly to the material. That division is the whole subject of the work.

sections.heading: Surface
sections.body:
Building the Surface

Foundation: preparing the surface.

Custom wood panels are prepared and layered with gypsum, lime, and cementitious plasters, creating the foundation for each piece and establishing the physical depth of the work.

• Wood panel
• Gypsum · lime
• Cementitious plaster

sections.heading: Layering
sections.body:
Layering & Material

A surface that records its own making.

Successive layers of mineral-based materials are applied, carved, and rebuilt. Each addition and subtraction creates a stratified surface that records the history of its own making.

• Mineral layers
• Carved
• Rebuilt

sections.heading: Color
sections.body:
Color & Light

Pigment worked in, with metal catching light.

Hand-mixed pigments are worked directly into the plaster, while subtle copper or brass gilding catches changing light, revealing new depth and texture as the surface evolves.

• Hand-mixed pigment
• Copper gilding
• Shifts with light

sections.heading: Erosion
sections.body:
Erosion & Discovery

What's carved away stays visible.

The surface is sanded, scraped, and excavated, exposing hidden layers beneath. Rather than covering imperfections, the process embraces them as part of the final composition.

• Sanded
• Excavated
• Imperfection kept

sections.heading: Finished
sections.body:
The Finished Work

Architecture, material, and time.

Each piece becomes a tactile convergence of architecture, material, and time — a contemporary work shaped through traditional techniques and guided by the balance between control and discovery.

• Traditional technique
• Contemporary form
• Control & chance
Let's connect to discuss a current piece, future project, or commissioned work.

sections.heading: I build the order. The material supplies the entropy.
sections.body:
Isaac Anderson makes cast sculpture and mixed-media relief in cement, plaster, and steel. He works between two studios — Southern California and Southern Kentucky — and the split shows up in the work: one half built to tolerance, the other left to weather.

Each piece begins as a controlled form and is finished by processes he doesn't direct: hydration, pigment migration, hairline cracking, and the slow ageing that continues in whatever room the work ends up in.
He works to commission for lobbies, hospitality interiors, and private collections, and keeps a small number of available works in the catalogue at any time.

sections.heading: Artist statement
sections.body:
I am drawn to the relationship between order and entropy—to surfaces that bear the marks of time rather than conceal them.

Through layered plasters, mineral pigments, and architectural materials, I seek moments where decay becomes revelation and history becomes tangible. Each work is an invitation to slow down, look closely, and discover the stories held within its layers.
